The problem behind
the request.

In the fictional Riverbend Licensing Support Unit, faults arrive by email, phone and spreadsheet. Staff cannot reliably see who owns a request, coordinators re-enter information, and tickets can close without confirmation that service has been restored.

The scenario supports the operationalisation of a new business system without modelling weapons licensing decisions, applicant records or police procedures.

The BA response

  • Map the hand-offs and validate the underlying assumptions.
  • Define measurable outcomes and prioritised requirements.
  • Design the controls, then demonstrate the complete workflow.
  • Test the solution and plan a controlled, measurable pilot.

Tools: stakeholder analysis, swimlanes, gap analysis, user stories, traceability, risk assessment, web prototype and a Microsoft 365 delivery blueprint.

What this project proves

It demonstrates an end-to-end BA method and a tested prototype. The discovery findings and baseline figures are invented inputs for the exercise.

It does not claim real stakeholder consultation, an approved QPS design, production security, a live Microsoft 365 deployment or realised operational savings. Production controls are recorded as release gates.
